name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
description: Eczema is a non-contagious, inflammatory skin condition that causes dry, red, itchy, and irritated patches of skin. It commonly flares up on the elbows, behind the knees, hands, and face.
common_symptoms: Dry, cracked, sensitive, and itchy skin
Red or brownish-gray patches (may look purple, grayish, or darker brown on deeper skin tones)
Small raised bumps that may leak clear fluid when scratched and crust over
Thickened, leathery skin from chronic rubbing and scratching (lichenification)
causes: A weakened skin barrier that allows moisture to escape and irritants/allergens to enter
Overactive immune response triggered by genetics and environmental allergens
risk_factors: Personal or family history of eczema, asthma, or hay fever (atopic triad)
Cold, dry weather or extreme heat and humidity
Harsh soaps, detergents, fragrances, and wool or synthetic fabrics
Psychological stress and lack of sleep
first_aid: Apply a cool, damp compress to soothe intense itchiness
Apply a generous layer of fragrance-free moisturizer or petroleum jelly immediately after a warm bath
Trim fingernails short to prevent skin damage from nighttime scratching
precautions: Take short (5 to 10 minute) lukewarm baths instead of hot showers
Moisturize skin within 3 minutes of bathing to lock in hydration
Use mild, unscented cleansers and fragrance-free laundry detergents
home_care: Keep skin constantly moisturized with plain ointments or thick creams
Use a humidifier in dry indoor environments
Avoid known personal food or contact triggers
do_not: DO NOT take long, steaming hot showers or baths that strip natural oils
DO NOT scratch or rub patches aggressively with fingernails or rough towels
DO NOT use heavily scented soaps, antibacterial soaps, or bubble baths
DO NOT apply strong steroid creams without a doctor's guidance
red_flags: Skin develops golden honey-colored crusts or pus blisters (secondary bacterial infection like impetigo)
Rapid spread of painful small blisters with fever (eczema herpeticum - medical emergency)
Spreading redness, warmth, swelling, and fever
when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor or dermatologist if your eczema is painful, causes sleepless nights, spreads rapidly, or shows signs of infection like oozing yellow fluid or pus.
prevention: Moisturize skin at least twice a day every day
Identify and avoid harsh chemical cleaners, synthetic fabrics, and irritants
Manage stress and maintain a consistent sleep schedule

sources.title: Atopic Dermatitis: Overview - American Academy of Dermatology
